blogs.title: When a ‘Big’ Post‑Cervical Mass is Not an Ovarian Cancer: Decoding CA‑125 in Pregnancy
blogs.description: This post dives into the diagnostic pitfalls of interpreting CA‑125 during pregnancy. Using the case of a 40‑year‑old null‑iparous woman with two huge abdominal masses, we explore how CA‑125 can spike for benign reasons such as decidualized endometriomas, uterine leiomyoma degeneration, and even physiological pregnancy peaks—highlighting serial testing, trend interpretation, and the limits of a single cut‑off.

blogs.title: Imaging on the Fly: Choosing Ultrasound vs. Non‑Contrast MRI for Masses in Pregnancy
blogs.description: A practical guide to the safe imaging toolbox for complex abdominal masses during pregnancy. We walk through the decision tree used in the case: why transvaginal‑based color Doppler, pelvic bimanual exam, and a 1.5‑T non‑contrast MRI were selected; when to avoid gadolinium; and how imaging findings shape surgical versus expectant management.

blogs.title: Endometrioma vs. Fibroid: The Role of Bimanual Examination and Differential Diagnosis
blogs.description: A deep dive into how a meticulous bimanual exam, complemented by imaging, can tease apart a decidualized endometrioma from a cystic‑degenerating leiomyoma. We review texture, mobility, and relationship to surrounding structures, using the case’s two distinct masses to illustrate the importance of the physical exam in the absence of definitive imaging.

blogs.title: Surgery in Second‑Trimester Pregnancy: When and How to Perform Myomectomy Safely
blogs.description: Charting the risk–benefit analysis that led to a selective upper‑myomectomy in the 21‑week pregnancy. This post outlines the criteria for operative intervention—mass‑related pain, dyspnea, risk of torsion/necrosis—along with operative planning: uterine incision type, fetal heart monitoring, intra‑operative progesterone, prophylactic antibiotics, and postoperative anemia management.

blogs.title: Planning Delivery after Massive Pelvic Fibroids: Cesarean vs. Vaginal Birth
blogs.description: Examining the evidence that informs mode‑of‑delivery decisions when large uterine fibroids persist. We discuss the impact of mass size, location (posterior intramural vs. pedunculated), anticipated obstacles to the birth canal, and how the case’s elective cesarean on the prior laparotomy scar balanced scar integrity against potential uterine rupture.

blogs.title: Post‑Myomectomy Anemia in Pregnancy: Prevention, Recognition, and Management
blogs.description: A focused look at peri‑operative anemia in pregnant patients undergoing myomectomy. We cover iron‑deficiency screening, transfusion thresholds, iron‑carboxymaltose use, and the role of intra‑operative blood loss estimation, drawing lessons from the patient’s transfusion‑dependent course following the excision of a vascular pedunculated leiomyoma.
